frontier.hypothesis: The floor-2 residual (final-callback jalr delay-slot fill) is the SAME site s2's H6 found closable only via `volatile s32 *p` -- an IRQ-callback-installed function's own single-read test-and-clear of a flag it owns could qualify as a fourth catalogued use-site shape under legitimate-volatile-interrupt-touched, closing the last 2 instructions with zero further search once ruled on.
frontier.mechanism: policy/ruling question, not a GCC pass
frontier.next_probe: File a ruling-request citing memory/grind/_exeque/rejected/volatile-D_8009BE7C-guard-clear.c, hypotheses.md H6, src/display.c's DMACallback(2, _exeque) IRQ-install site, and the fact that the floor has been at 2/187 (down from 12) for two consecutive sessions with the permuter search space now exhausted (>=20k iterations, 0 finds).

frontier.hypothesis: A non-volatile pure-C lever for the jalr-delay-slot fill may still exist outside plain-C statement reordering of the final block or random permuter mutation -- e.g. restructuring the surrounding do-while loop's exit path, or moving the guard-and-clear block relative to the SetIntrMask(D_8009BF84) call that precedes it.
frontier.mechanism: GCC 2.7.2 reorg.c fill_simple_delay_slots (tools/gcc-2.7.2/reorg.c:2861-3027) excludes a trial insn only via ordinary resource-conflict analysis (mark_set_resources/mark_referenced_resources) between the jalr and the candidate store -- volatile forces a conflict by treating the MEM as touching all memory; the open question is whether any OTHER C-level restructuring changes the resource-conflict computation without volatile
frontier.next_probe: Read tools/gcc-2.7.2/reorg.c's mark_set_resources/mark_referenced_resources (called from fill_simple_delay_slots) to find what non-volatile conditions could make the jalr's own resource footprint (mark_set_resources on a CALL_INSN, reorg.c ~3072-3079) conflict with the preceding store; try moving SetIntrMask(D_8009BF84) or restructuring the enclosing if to change what the jalr's CALL_INSN resource set includes.

frontier.hypothesis: The do-while(0)-wrapped chassis in candidate.c (unchanged since s4, re-confirmed this session) remains the best known starting point for any future session on this function -- re-deriving it from scratch would waste a session, and re-seeding its jalr-delay-slot permuter search space without a structural change first would also waste a session per the ledger's CHASSIS RULE.
frontier.next_probe: Next session should apply memory/grind/_exeque/candidate.c verbatim (sandbox floor 2/187, confirmed this session), then EITHER file the ruling-request above OR attempt a genuinely different structural rewrite of the final-callback block (not yet tried: restructuring around the loop-exit condition, or moving SetIntrMask relative to the guard) before any further permuter campaign on this exact residual.
